alignments.note: Indefinite article belongs to the noun that licenses it (rule 15); head on the lexeme-bearing noun.
Superscription lamed rendered 'of'.
Vocative divine name; the ASV writes no 'O' here, so nothing further is placed (rule 36).
Finite verb with its subject pronoun and auxiliary (rule 17); the 'upon' is the preposition the English verb's valency needs to reach its bare object suffix, so it joins the verb's unit (rule 44).
Object suffix keeps only the pronoun written for it (rule 18).
Light verb plus complement heads on the complement (rule 44).
Cohortative/paragogic he on the imperative has no English realization (rule 32); MACULA does not tag it Sd, so the directive-he reading does not arise.
Rule 44 reads הַאֲזִין → 'Give ear unto' as one unit headed on 'ear'; the 'unto' reaches the bare object קוֹלִי.
Cohortative/paragogic he, as at s008 (rule 32).
Temporal preposition before an infinitive construct takes the 'when' (rule 52).
Suffix on the infinitive construct is its subject and takes the English subject pronoun (rule 18).
Suffix is 2fs in the projection while the ASV writes 'thee'; the pronoun written is what is aligned.

review_notes: Both Sh tokens are cohortative/paragogic he on imperatives, not the Sd directive he, so both are unrepresented under rule 32.
'upon thee' and 'ear unto' both divide by rule 44: the supplied preposition reaching the verb's own object stays with the verb, while the suffix and the noun keep their own words.

alignments.note: Volitive frame belongs to the verb whose mood it renders (rule 17); 'set forth' is a lexical verb with its phrasal particle, headed on the verb (rule 44). Discontinuous around the subject under rule 25.
Comparative 'as' supplied before a bare nominal belongs to that nominal (rule 33); it is never the head.
Preposition on a construct noun rendered by one English word fuses, headed on the construct noun (rules 30, 23).
Suffix on the construct noun takes its own pronoun and is no part of the fusion (rule 30).
Construct noun with a supplied 'the' (rule 29); 'lifting up' is its one rendering, headed on the lexeme-bearing word (rule 31).
Nomen rectum takes the relational 'of' (rule 19), discontinuous around the possessive.

The chain is rendered attributively (rule 28), so the construct noun is the English head and takes the single supplied 'the' (rule 29); the supplied comparative 'as' stands before the phrase this nominal opens and goes to it (rule 33). Unit discontinuous around 'evening' under rule 25.
Rectum rendered attributively as 'evening' (rule 28).

review_notes: The marginal 'Or, oblation' was read and set aside; the printed text governs (rule 38).
Competing reading on t018 'the': it could be given to the rectum as the word it stands before, but rule 29 places a chain's single supplied determiner on the construct noun in either English order.

alignments.note: Cohortative/paragogic he on the imperative (rule 32).
Vocative noun takes the supplied 'O' into its own unit (rule 36).
Indefinite article belongs to the noun that licenses it (rule 15).
The ASV recasts the dative as 'before'; the preposition takes the word written for it (rule 11).
Cohortative/paragogic he, as at s002 (rule 32).
The ASV promotes the object of עַל to the direct object of 'Keep', leaving the preposition's own relation unstated (rule 40).
Construct noun with a supplied 'the', no article morpheme being present (rule 29).
Nomen rectum takes the 'of' (rule 19), discontinuous around the possessive.

review_notes: Both imperatives carry an emphatic he with no English of its own; both are unrepresented under rule 32.
עַל is left unrepresented because the ASV writes 'Keep the door' with a bare object, spending no word on the preposition's relation (rule 40).

alignments.note: Supplied quantifying determiner 'any' joins the noun's unit, no כֹּל or other determiner morpheme standing in the phrase (rule 15); the head stays on the noun. Discontinuous around 'evil' under rule 25.
Purpose lamed before an infinitive construct takes the written 'To' (rule 52).
The ASV writes 'of' for this preposition; a present function morpheme takes the word whose sense it carries (rule 11).
This is the preposition אֵת 'with' (H854), not the object marker (rule 16).
Articleless participle modifying an explicit noun, recast as a relative clause; the supplied relative joins the attributive's unit and the head goes to the lexeme-bearing word (rule 41).
The ASV writes no 'of' here, so rule 19 has nothing to place.
Volitive frame with its subject pronoun belongs to the verb whose mood it renders (rule 17); discontinuous around the negative under rule 25.

review_notes: s015 could alternatively be read as a substantival participle under rule 46; either way the supplied 'that' stays in the participle's unit and the head is 'work'.
'let me not eat' divides with the negative on בַל and the whole volitive frame, including the subject pronoun, on the finite verb (rules 17, 35).

alignments.note: Jussive frame belongs to the verb whose mood it renders (rule 17); discontinuous around the subject under rule 25.
Anarthrous substantival adjective takes the supplied 'the' into its own unit, headed on the word carrying the lexeme (rule 46).

Referential/impersonal 'it' answering to no morpheme; rule 20 marks such a pronoun added, reserving the construction-supplied frame for the presentative 'there'. ASV italic corroborates and decides nothing (rule 7).
Nominal predicate of a verbless clause takes the construction-supplied copula, modal auxiliary included (rules 20, 49); the indefinite article is the noun's own (rule 15).
Jussive frame with the subject pronoun realizing the verb's own person and number (rule 17).
Second impersonal 'it', added on the same terms as t006 (rule 20).
Nominal predicate takes the copula (rule 20); the supplied comparative 'as' stands before this bare nominal and belongs to it (rule 33), never as head.
The ASV recasts the construct relation with 'upon', which belongs to the nomen rectum (rule 19); the supplied 'the' determines that noun (rules 15, 29).
Jussive frame with the verb (rule 17), discontinuous around the negative and the subject under rule 25.
Supplied object pronoun with no object morpheme in the clause; rule 44 marks such a pronoun added rather than folding it into the verb.

The adverbial anchor of this verbless clause takes the verb the ASV writes where the copula would stand, 'shall ... continue' rendering its own 'still' (rules 20, 49); rule 20 already reads עוֹד as such an anchor. Discontinuous under rule 25.
The waw takes the connective the ASV wrote for it; a waw rendered 'even' is never added (rule 14), and כִּי already holds its own 'For' (rule 51).

review_notes: The two marginal notes ('Or, still is my prayer against their wickedness', 'Or, calamities') were read and set aside; the printed text governs (rule 38).

The italicized 'it shall be' twice divides into an added referential 'it' and a construction-supplied copula joining the nominal predicate (rule 20); a competing reading would take all three words as one added frame, but that would leave the verbless clauses' copula unaccounted.

Materially different reading available at s015/s016: 'even' could be taken as the rendering of עוֹד and 'continue' as a supplied lexical verb, but that leaves the waw unrendered and supplies a predicate no morpheme carries, so the division above was preferred.

alignments.note: Passive verb with its auxiliary and particle, headed on the lexical verb (rules 24, 44).
The ASV writes 'by' for this preposition (rule 11).
Construct noun with a supplied 'the', no article morpheme being present (rule 29).
Nomen rectum takes the 'of' (rule 19) together with the supplied determiner standing before its own word (rules 15, 29).
Finite verb with its subject pronoun and auxiliary (rule 17).
Stative verb rendered by subject pronoun, copula and adjective; the head is the word carrying the lexeme (rules 17, 44).

review_notes: 'the sides of the rock' takes its two supplied determiners on the two nouns they stand before, no article morpheme standing in the phrase (rules 15, 29).

alignments.note: The ASV recasts the comparative phrase as a clause and writes 'As when' for the one comparative morpheme; both words are its single rendering, headed on the word carrying the comparison (rules 55, 24). The competing reading takes 'when' as an added subordinator under rule 55, but the clause has this comparative standing over it.
Anarthrous substantival participle takes the supplied 'one' that makes it an English noun phrase, headed on the lexeme-bearing word (rule 46).
The second coordinated participle takes only what is written, the antecedent 'one' being written once (rules 46, 22).
The ASV promotes the object of the preposition to the direct object of 'cleaveth', leaving its relation unstated (rule 40).
Assimilated article is a real token and takes the written 'the' (rule 12).
Passive verb with its copula, headed on the lexical verb (rule 24).
The ASV writes 'at' for this preposition (rule 11).
Construct noun with a supplied 'the' (rule 29).
Nomen rectum takes the 'of' (rule 19).

review_notes: The bracketed article at s006 is a real token assimilated into the pointed preposition and takes the written 'the' (rule 12), while the preposition itself is unrepresented because its object is promoted to a direct object (rule 40).
'As when' is read as one rendering of כְּמוֹ; the alternative marks 'when' added under rule 55, which was set aside because a connective morpheme does stand over the clause.

alignments.note: Prepositional predicate of a verbless clause takes the construction-supplied copula on the preposition (rule 49).
Vocative divine name takes the supplied 'O' into its own unit (rule 36).
The base noun of the title takes 'the Lord', the supplied determiner joining it under rule 15 (rule 57).
The 1cs suffix of the divine title is lexicalized in the name and the ASV writes no possessive for it (rule 57).
Finite verb with its fronted auxiliary and subject pronoun (rule 17); 'take refuge' is a light verb with its complement, headed on the complement (rule 44).

The ASV recasts the verb as 'leave ... destitute'; both words are its one rendering, headed on the word carrying the lexeme by rule 44's subtraction, since 'leave' alone writes no emptying. Discontinuous around the object under rule 25.

review_notes: The marginal 'Or, pour thou not out my life' was read and set aside; the printed 'leave not my soul destitute' governs (rule 38).
Competing head at s013: 'leave' is defensible if the phrase is read as a plain verb with an adjectival complement, but the subtraction test of rules 31 and 44 puts the lexeme on 'destitute'.
The title divides by rule 57: יהוה takes 'O Jehovah', אֲדֹנָ takes 'the Lord', and its lexicalized suffix is unrepresented.

alignments.note: Preposition on a construct noun rendered by one English word fuses, headed on the construct noun (rules 30, 23); the second 'from' is the same morpheme's scope rewritten over the coordinated member and joins its discontinuous unit (rules 25, 33). Target head is the first occurrence.
Supplied determiner joins the noun it determines (rules 15, 29).
The Hebrew writes the relative clause asyndetically with a written antecedent, so the supplied relative subordinates a clause no morpheme reaches and is added (rules 46, 55).
Finite verb with its subject pronoun and auxiliary (rule 17).
Construct noun with a supplied 'the' (rule 29).
Nomen rectum takes the 'of' (rule 19); the anarthrous substantival participle takes the supplied 'the' that makes it an English noun phrase (rule 46).
Inner rectum takes its own 'of' (rule 19).

review_notes: מִידֵי פַח is read as a preposition fused with its construct noun under rule 30, the pair rendered by the single 'from' and headed on יָד; the competing reading marks יָד unrepresented, which rule 30 forbids where one English word stands for the pair.
The second 'from' at t013 is the distributed scope of that one preposition over the coordinated member (rules 25, 33), not a second word for the waw.
'which' is added: the antecedent is written and no relative morpheme stands in the Hebrew clause (rules 46, 55).

alignments.note: Jussive frame belongs to the verb whose mood it renders (rule 17); discontinuous around the subject under rule 25.
The ASV writes 'into' for this preposition (rule 11).
The emphatic possessive belongs whole to the suffix, headed on the pronoun (rule 18).
Anarthrous substantival adjective takes the supplied 'the', headed on the word carrying the lexeme (rule 46).
The adverb is rendered by 'withal' (rule 11).

'Whilst that' is one subordinating rendering of the single connective morpheme, headed on the word the connective itself is (rule 55).
The ASV renders the verb 'escape'; the marginal literal gloss is set aside (rule 38).

'Whilst that' is taken as one rendering of עַד; the competing reading marks 'that' added under rule 55, but a connective morpheme does stand in the clause.
